title: Hidden Leaf Colors: Parent Guide
endLine: Green leaves hide yellow all summer; fall just uncovers it.

scenes.tts: Where does the yellow in a fall leaf come from? Start with a fresh green leaf beside a yellow one. A sample coffee-filter strip can help you answer that question.
scenes.caption: Where does the yellow in a fall leaf come from? Start with a fresh green leaf beside a yellow one. A sample coffee-filter strip can help you answer that question.
scenes.visual: Show a fresh green leaf and a yellow fall leaf beside each other on a bright tabletop. Hold the question on screen as a sample white coffee-filter strip slides in below the leaves.
scenes.narration: Where does the yellow in a fall leaf come from? Start with a fresh green leaf beside a yellow one. A sample coffee-filter strip can help you answer that question.

scenes.visual: The leaf and filter-strip drawing gently dims into the background while clean bold title text appears centered: 'Hidden Leaf Colors' with a small subtitle 'Parent guide'.

scenes.tts: Your child gets to make a guess, look closely at leaf prints, and sort leaves by color. You can use the sample strip together to talk about a color you could not see before.
scenes.caption: Your child gets to make a guess, look closely at leaf prints, and sort leaves by color. You can use the sample strip together to talk about a color you could not see before.
scenes.visual: On the same tabletop, unfold a sheet of paper to reveal a green print. Slide fallen leaves into small groups as a notebook opens beside them.
scenes.narration: Your child gets to make a guess, look closely at leaf prints, and sort leaves by color. You can use the sample strip together to talk about a color you could not see before.

scenes.tts: This activity uses no alcohol. Gather white paper, a spoon, a fresh green leaf, and fallen leaves in different colors. If you go outside, go with your child. Collect where you have permission, away from roads, and take leaves only from plants you know.
scenes.caption: This activity uses no alcohol. Gather white paper, a spoon, a fresh green leaf, and fallen leaves in different colors. If you go outside, go with your child. Collect where you have permission, away from roads, and take leaves only from plants you know.
scenes.visual: Show white paper, a spoon and green, yellow and red leaves on the tabletop. A sketch on the open notebook shows an adult and child collecting fallen leaves well away from a road.
scenes.narration: This activity uses no alcohol. Gather white paper, a spoon, a fresh green leaf, and fallen leaves in different colors. If you go outside, go with your child. Collect where you have permission, away from roads, and take leaves only from plants you know.

scenes.tts: Avoid poison ivy. Dress for the sun and weather, and check for ticks afterward. Keep small leaf pieces away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking. Never taste the leaves, and wash hands with soap afterward.
scenes.caption: Avoid poison ivy. Dress for the sun and weather, and check for ticks afterward. Keep small leaf pieces away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking. Never taste the leaves, and wash hands with soap afterward.
scenes.visual: Keep the notebook in place. Use simple drawings for sun, appropriate clothing and checking for ticks. On the table, slide small leaf bits out of reach, then show soap and running water.
scenes.narration: Avoid poison ivy. Dress for the sun and weather, and check for ticks afterward. Keep small leaf pieces away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking. Never taste the leaves, and wash hands with soap afterward.

scenes.tts: Show the green and yellow leaves side by side. Ask your child, "Which colors do you think will rub off onto the paper?" Have them draw or write a guess. Then fold a sheet of white paper over the green leaf.
scenes.caption: Show the green and yellow leaves side by side. Ask your child, "Which colors do you think will rub off onto the paper?" Have them draw or write a guess. Then fold a sheet of white paper over the green leaf.
scenes.visual: Place the green and yellow leaves beside the notebook. Show a pencil marking a guess. Put the green leaf inside a fold of white paper.
scenes.narration: Show the green and yellow leaves side by side. Ask your child, "Which colors do you think will rub off onto the paper?" Have them draw or write a guess. Then fold a sheet of white paper over the green leaf.

scenes.tts: Have your child rub the folded paper with the back of a spoon. Keep rubbing until a green print shows through. Repeat with a yellow leaf and a red leaf. Ask, "Which colors came off onto the paper?" Compare the prints with their guess.
scenes.caption: Have your child rub the folded paper with the back of a spoon. Keep rubbing until a green print shows through. Repeat with a yellow leaf and a red leaf. Ask, "Which colors came off onto the paper?" Compare the prints with their guess.
scenes.visual: A drawn hand rubs the folded paper with the back of a spoon. Unfold it and arrange the prints beside the leaves. Return to the note with the guess.
scenes.narration: Have your child rub the folded paper with the back of a spoon. Keep rubbing until a green print shows through. Repeat with a yellow leaf and a red leaf. Ask, "Which colors came off onto the paper?" Compare the prints with their guess.

scenes.tts: Put the fallen leaves back on the table. Have your child sort them into piles by color. Ask them to count the leaves in each pile. Keep the green leaf and a yellow leaf nearby for the comparison.
scenes.caption: Put the fallen leaves back on the table. Have your child sort them into piles by color. Ask them to count the leaves in each pile. Keep the green leaf and a yellow leaf nearby for the comparison.
scenes.visual: Slide the fallen leaves into red and yellow piles, with one small tally per leaf. Leave the green leaf and a yellow leaf beside the notebook.
scenes.narration: Put the fallen leaves back on the table. Have your child sort them into piles by color. Ask them to count the leaves in each pile. Keep the green leaf and a yellow leaf nearby for the comparison.

scenes.tts: Look at this drawing of a sample coffee-filter strip. Fresh green spinach can make a wide green band with a thin yellow one above it. Ask, "Where do you see yellow on the strip and on the fall leaf?"
scenes.caption: Look at this drawing of a sample coffee-filter strip. Fresh green spinach can make a wide green band with a thin yellow one above it. Ask, "Where do you see yellow on the strip and on the fall leaf?"
scenes.visual: Slide a drawn coffee-filter strip beside the green and yellow leaves. Label it “Example strip.” Show a wide green band below a thin yellow band, and trace a line from the yellow band to the yellow leaf.
scenes.narration: Look at this drawing of a sample coffee-filter strip. Fresh green spinach can make a wide green band with a thin yellow one above it. Ask, "Where do you see yellow on the strip and on the fall leaf?"

scenes.tts: The yellow was already in the green leaf. Here is a follow-up question for you before your child asks it. Was a red fall leaf also hiding its red under the green all summer?
scenes.caption: The yellow was already in the green leaf. Here is a follow-up question for you before your child asks it. Was a red fall leaf also hiding its red under the green all summer?
scenes.visual: The dry paper strip with its wide green band and thin yellow top band slides onto a clean plate next to a yellow fall leaf, with a soft matching highlight connecting both yellows. Then a bright red maple leaf slides in beside them, and a bold question card appears: 'Was red also hidden under green all summer?'
scenes.narration: The yellow was already in the green leaf. Here is a follow-up question for you before your child asks it. Was a red fall leaf also hiding its red under the green all summer?

scenes.visual: Hold cleanly on the question card beside the green, yellow, and red leaves, with only a slow, gentle progress bar gliding across the bottom edge so the parent has quiet thinking time.

scenes.tts: Usually, no, and that makes a great follow-up talk. Yellow pigments sit inside green leaves all summer until green chlorophyll fades in fall. Most reds are made new in fall from trapped sugars, showing two ways fall colors appear.
scenes.caption: Usually, no, and that makes a great follow-up talk. Yellow pigments sit inside green leaves all summer until green chlorophyll fades in fall. Most reds are made new in fall from trapped sugars, showing two ways fall colors appear.
scenes.visual: Clean schematic reveal over the same tabletop. Left side: a green leaf gently fades its green chlorophyll layer away to reveal the yellow layer already underneath ('Yellow: hidden all summer'). Right side: a red leaf lights up with small bright dots representing sugars turning into red pigment in fall ('Most red: made new in fall'). Both gently settle beside the finished coffee-filter strip.
scenes.narration: Usually, no, and that makes a great follow-up talk. Yellow pigments sit inside green leaves all summer until green chlorophyll fades in fall. Most reds are made new in fall from trapped sugars, showing two ways fall colors appear.
